issue.title: [TwigBridge] allow null for $message of filter method `trans`
issue.body:
| Q             | A
| ------------- | ---
| Branch?       | 5.0
| Bug fix?      | yes
| New feature?  | no
| Deprecations? | no
| Tickets       | Fix #37931
| License       | MIT

With Symfony 5.0, filter method `trans` of Symfony Twig Bridge does not allow null values for `$message` parameter anymore, breaking backward compatibility. See also #37931. The included commit provides a fix to this BC break by allowing null values again.

body:
Passing `null` values to the translator was never supported : https://github.com/symfony/symfony/blob/4.4/src/Symfony/Component/Translation/TranslatorInterface.php#L29

It worked because we couldn't enforce it but it never was a supported use of the translator.

> Passing `null` values to the translator was never supported : https://github.com/symfony/symfony/blob/4.4/src/Symfony/Component/Translation/TranslatorInterface.php#L29
> 
> It worked because we couldn't enforce it but it never was a supported use of the translator.

Please have a look at `Symfony\Contracts\Translation\TranslatorTrait`, even there null values are allowed. And most (all?) implementations of `Symfony\Contracts\Translation\TranslatorInterface` also allow null values. However, it is a BC break. Please be reasonable.

Even Nicolas admits that "implementations are allowed to accept null, following the LSP" (see [comment](https://github.com/symfony/contracts/commit/120a869f132d9f7f10a7cb79918ae45b1f1d1588#r41595170)).
Well, the Symfony translator use `inheritdoc` meaning it also clams to only support strings.

> Well, the Symfony translator use `inheritdoc` meaning it also clams to only support strings.

And it yet allows null values. Please look at the code. The type of the to-be-translated parameter is `?string` and the method explicitly checks for null values.

[Translator](https://github.com/symfony/symfony/blob/efdc35c3871440b9f520ed1490f40daf871d1a06/src/Symfony/Component/Translation/Translator.php#L196)
[TranslatorTrait](https://github.com/symfony/symfony/blob/efdc35c3871440b9f520ed1490f40daf871d1a06/src/Symfony/Contracts/Translation/TranslatorTrait.php#L44)

You're right, I checked the 4.4 version and not the last one. I'm not sure why it was decided to allow `null` for concrete implementations and not in the interface.

The problem is: we can't change the typing of the interface since it would be a BC break, and since the translation extension claim to support all implementations of the interface, modifying the extension to allow could lead to error case when coupled with implementations that support `null`, it wouldn't necessarily be a problem but could lead to harder to debug errors.

Thank you for your reply, @jvasseur. I get your point, well, somehow. We _already have_ a BC break here, in the Twig Bridge, because null values were allowed before, but now they are not anymore.

How would loosen the type declaration from `string` to `?string` in the interface lead to BC breaks, especially while the implementations disregard it anyway? Consequently, the implementations would have to be tighten to only allow `string` as well, but _this_ would really lead to _further_ BC breaks.

However, I don't care too much about the translator interface, because the Twig Bridge doesn't implement the interface at all: it just _uses_ the interface for delegation. So the easiest and probably cleanest solution would be to allow null values in the Twig Bridge again to fix the BC break, and then to explicitly check for null values here, for an early out, in order to not pass possible null values to the actual translator, which currently still allows null values as well, but might follow the specification of the "not-null interface" one day.

I have added a commit for this additional aspect of explicitly checking for null values in order to not pass them to the actual translator.

> How would loosen the type declaration from `string` to `?string` in the interface lead to BC breaks, especially while the implementations disregard it anyway? Consequently, the implementations would have to be tighten to only allow `string` as well, but _this_ would really lead to _further_ BC breaks.

This would break BC if someone was implementing the interface without loosening the type to allow null. In this case, if we change the interface they would end up with an implementation that doesn't accept all the types that the interface accepts witch is a LSP violation.

> However, I don't care too much about the translator interface, because the Twig Bridge doesn't implement the interface at all: it just uses the interface for delegation. So the easiest and probably cleanest solution would be to allow null values in the Twig Bridge again to fix the BC break, and then to explicitly check for null values here, for an early out, in order to not pass possible null values to the actual translator, which currently still allows null values as well, but might follow the specification of the "not-null interface" one day.

I agree with you here, if we do something, it has to be in the Twig bridge
